title: Fleet Rung 39 — THE SWAP NET: the DEX learns to route. The owner directed the DEX to handle swaps across as many networks as possible, FIRST for STEEM/HIVE/BLURT and the coins we already work with (pegs and wrappers included), opposing grids on our side of the book, and a networked arbitrage market for the agents — with real swaps to real value, never a fake. The router desk (dex-router.cjs) now measures every reachable venue hourly, quotes a 12-route catalog with honest verdicts (LIVE-KEYED / GATED-KEYS / GATED-CAPITAL / C-GATE-OPERATOR / NO-RAIL / INTERNAL-SIM — every gated route names its unlock), runs the arb net with a FLOOR law and a 1.5% peg-drift halt, and plans the counter-grids anchored to the CEX-implied fair price with Avellaneda inventory skew.

queries.Q51_which_real_rails_exist_today: A 20+ query sweep + live API probes (MEXC, Gate, Binance, HTX, SimpleSwap, Swapzone, Exolix, Trocador, BlockTrades, Hive-Engine) produced the rails matrix: CEX native-chain deposits are the only real-size path (MEXC/Binance/Gate live for STEEM+HIVE, HTX for SBD); instant swappers are API-keyed and thin; BLURT has NO rail. Encoded as R7/R8/R9 (C-GATE-OPERATOR) and R10 (NO-RAIL).
queries.Q52_why_lead_lag_and_not_bridge_arbitrag: Makarov-Schoar (JFE 2020): cross-venue spreads persist precisely because transfers are non-atomic — and with ~$20-70 liquid, a split-inventory arb across a CEX and the internal market is structurally impossible (one HTX taker fee + withdrawal exceeds the typical spread). The desk therefore implements the lead-lag architecture: quote BOTH sides of the internal market around the CEX-implied fair price (the counter-grid anchor) so the CEX's head start becomes our maker edge, and book true-arb candidates only as FOK legs with the 2×(capture+0.4%) floor.
queries.Q53_what_are_the_opposing_grids: market-exec already ladders around the local touch (its own side). The counter-grid is the OTHER side: anchored to the CEX-implied fair (not the local mid), spaced by max(vol×0.1, 0.4% round-trip floor), skewed ±50bps by inventory share (Avellaneda-style: STEEM-heavy inventory shifts the whole ladder down to favor sells), sized by the 0.9 commit law under the 1.25 STEEM per-level policy cap. Booked PLAN-OWNER-GATED-NOT-BROADCAST — the signing stays with market-exec/grid-beat.
queries.Q54_how_do_the_sim_tokens_reach_real_val: honestly: SAOS/USDS/WSTEEM/WTRX live in the SIM book (labeled SIM, real-money-audited, zero keys). The corridor is R11: SAOS→USDS→WSTEEM on the internal AMM (quoted live from the mirror with 1%-pool impact), then the WSTEEM→STEEM peg-out rail (armed-needs-sovereign-identity, dex/agent.json), then R7 (CEX rail) — and NOT ONE STEP of that corridor is promised as live until each gate opens. The SIM book is never laundered into realized P&L.

The net is therefore sharded by RAIL OWNER today (headcorner = the only keyed rail), and every arb row books its railOwner by name. The soldiers' lane into the net opens the day active key material exists (a booked rung, not a promise).
queries.Q56_when_does_the_money_arrive: the measured truth: the powerdown drip pays 2026-10-10T02:01:27 and weekly ×13 (470.84 SP measured rate). No 3-day lock is recorded in ANY estate book; this rung does not invent one. The desk's honest answer to 'everything working by tomorrow': the SWAP NET is measured, tested (62/62) and live TODAY; the profit converts when the drip lands and the gated routes unlock.
queries.Q57_what_does_open_to_more_networks_mean: the tier law: T0 = our internal books (steem internal keyed; SAOS AMM engine-gated), T1 = wrapped pools (Hive-Engine, ≤2% of pool depth per trade, peg-drift halt 1.5%), T2 = whitelisted external rails (CEX accounts for size; no-account exchangers only where measured live). Bridge-intent architecture (ERC-7683 / Dutch-auction resolvers / TSS networks) is the booked NEXT rung for the EVM/TRON/SOL doors — the deposit doors already watch (dex/watch.json); signing identities are the missing gate, named, not hidden.
queries.Q58_what_proves_profit: the honest KPI chain: dex-router-history.jsonl (the edge time-series, born this rung) + market-grid-history.jsonl + fill-ledger fills = bps captured per unit of inventory risk. At our scale the dependable return is the drip converted into working inventory plus maker capture in chop; any projection above 0.5-2%/month on deployed liquid capital is fiction, and the books refuse fiction.
